chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he

was asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Beneficent is established upon the Throne' [20:5]. So he said: 'He is established upon everything, so there is not anything closer to Him than another thing.'

key_terms.اسْتَوَى: From istawā, meaning 'to be established, to be even, to be balanced' — used in the Quran regarding God's relation to the Throne; the Imam reinterprets it as encompassing all creation
key_terms.الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى: The Beneficent is established upon the Throne (Quran 20:5) — the Quranic phrase being interpreted
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne — in Islamic cosmology, the highest created station, often understood as the divine seat of dominion and sovereignty
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — standard formula of glorification appended to God's name in hadith literature

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the meaning of 'The Beneficent is upon the Throne' in Quran 20:5?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of Quran 20:5, where God is described as established upon the Throne (al-'Arsh). The Imam responded with a profound theological clarification: God's 'establishment' (istawa) is not spatially limited to the Throne, but encompasses all of existence — He is equally present to all things, so no thing is nearer to Him than any other. This response reflects the Shia theological approach of negating anthropomorphism (tashbih) while affirming divine transcendence: God's nearness is not a physical proximity but an ontological reality equally shared by all creation.
